instruction: Please create a user named "emily" with a password and set the password to expire in 30 days.

result.command: USERNAME="emily"; id "$USERNAME" &>/dev/null && PASS_STATUS=$(passwd -S "$USERNAME" | awk '{print $2}') && [ "$PASS_STATUS" = "P" ] && MAX_DAYS=$(chage -l "$USERNAME" | grep 'Maximum number of days' | awk -F: '{print $2}' | tr -d ' ') && [ "$MAX_DAYS" = "30" ] && echo 'User exists with password and 30-day expiry' || echo 'Check failed'

metadata.explanation: Task requires creating user 'emily' with a password and setting password expiration to 30 days. Evaluator uses 'id' to verify user exists, 'passwd -S' to verify password is set (status 'P' for password set, not 'L' for locked or 'NP' for no password), and 'chage -l' to verify maximum password age is set to 30 days. Note: Password value cannot be verified programmatically without authentication testing.

llm_judge_reasons: Complete verification: Instruction requires three things: (1) create user 'emily', (2) set a password, (3) set 30-day expiry. Evaluator correctly verifies all three requirements.
User existence check: 'id "$USERNAME"' correctly verifies user 'emily' exists on the system.

Password status check: 'PASS_STATUS=$(passwd -S "$USERNAME" | awk '{print $2}') && [ "$PASS_STATUS" = "P" ]' correctly verifies that a password is set (status 'P' means password set, not 'L' for locked or 'NP' for no password).

Password expiry check: 'chage -l "$USERNAME" | grep 'Maximum number of days' | awk -F: '{print $2}' | tr -d ' '' extracts max password days and '[ "$MAX_DAYS" = "30" ]' correctly verifies it equals 30.
Logic flow: Command uses proper bash chaining with && so all checks must pass before echoing success message. If any check fails, 'Check failed' is echoed.
State accessibility: All required system state (user account, password status, password aging) is accessible via standard Linux commands (id, passwd -S, chage -l).
Expected values: Include/exclude rules correctly match the command output ('User exists with password and 30-day expiry' for success, 'Check failed' for failure).
